A1_Definition_Context.definition: WAX describes the momentary willingness to act of an actor or segment. It functions as a bridge between utility logic (INU, KNU, IDN) and real behavior.
A1_Definition_Context.formal_basis: Hybrid function between Additivity and Complementarity, controlled by $\lambda \in [0,1]$

goals: Mapping the momentary willingness to act
Integration of context variables (UNS, KOM, INST)

A4_Axiomatics.description: The axiomatics of WAX comprise approximately 70–80 axioms.

Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.title: Context Dependency
Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.wording: WAX is always a function of Awareness, Utility Types (INU, KNU, IDN), Uncertainty, Complexity, Segment, and Institutions.
Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.formula: $WAX = f(AWX, INU, KNU, IDN, UNS, KOM, SEG, INST)$

Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.title: Salience Filter
Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.wording: Only utility types that are made salient by Awareness are considered in WAX. Non-salient utilities are equal to zero.

Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.title: Discounting by Uncertainty
Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.wording: Uncertainty reduces the contribution of a utility proportionally by a factor $\gamma$.

Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.title: Amplification by Complexity
Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.wording: Complexity can amplify or attenuate utility values by a factor $\delta$.

Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.title: Weighting Factor
Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.wording: Each utility type receives a weight $\alpha_i$; the sum of all $\alpha_i$ is 1.

Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.title: Momentary Willingness to Act
Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.wording: WAX exclusively maps the current state, not long-term utility structures.

Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.title: Non-Isolation
Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.wording: WAX cannot be calculated in isolation but always requires inputs from INU, KNU, IDN, and AWX.

Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.title: Dynamic Sensitivity
Cluster1_Basic_Conditions.wording: WAX is sensitive to small changes in AWX, UNS, and KOM.

Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.title: Hybrid Function
Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.wording: WAX is a weighted mixture of additive and complementary logic, controlled by the factor λ.

Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.title: Additive Border Case
Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.wording: If $\lambda = 0$, WAX follows additive logic and corresponds to an optimizing actor (Homo oeconomicus).

Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.title: Complementary Border Case
Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.wording: If $\lambda = 1$, WAX follows complementary logic, and behavior is blocked by the weakest component.

Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.title: Normal Mixed Form Case
Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.wording: In the normal case, λ is between 0 and 1, and WAX is a mixed form.

Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.title: Endogeneity of λ
Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.wording: The value of λ is endogenous and is determined by norm salience, identity, institutions, and complexity.

Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.title: Ambivalence Measure
Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.wording: The difference between the additive and complementary result is a measure of ambivalence.

Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.title: Path Dependence
Cluster2_Definition_Hybrid_Logic.wording: The current value of λ depends on its history (path dependence).

Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.title: Time Dependence
Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.wording: WAX changes over time due to learning, habituation, or norm erosion.

Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.title: Norm Salience
Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.wording: Salient norms increase the influence of collective and identity utility types.

Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.title: Emotional Amplification
Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.wording: Emotions modulate the weighting of individual utility types.

Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.title: Information Availability
Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.wording: More information reduces uncertainty and increases the effectiveness of utility.

Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.title: Social Proximity
Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.wording: Utilities from close social relationships have higher weights.

Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.title: Stress & Coping
Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.wording: Stress situations can distort utility processing; coping strategies act as a regulator.

Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.title: Time Horizon
Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.wording: Short-term utilities are over-proportionally weighted compared to long-term utilities.

Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.title: Context Vector
Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.wording: The context (political, cultural, ecological) modulates the entire WAX function.

Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.title: Technology Influence
Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.wording: Digital communication changes salience and accelerates norm diffusion.

Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.title: Social Comparison Processes
Cluster3_Influencing_Factors.wording: Willingness to act depends on comparison with relevant peers.

Cluster4_Functional_Logic.title: Additive Logic
Cluster4_Functional_Logic.wording: In the additive case, all salient weighted utilities are summed. This corresponds to the Homo oeconomicus.
Cluster4_Functional_Logic.formula: WAX^add = Σ (α_i * γ_i * δ_i * U_i * S_i)

Cluster4_Functional_Logic.title: Complementary Logic
Cluster4_Functional_Logic.wording: In the complementary case, the willingness to act is determined by the weakest component.
Cluster4_Functional_Logic.formula: WAX^compl = min(α_i * γ_i * δ_i * U_i * S_i)

Cluster4_Functional_Logic.title: Hybrid Logic
Cluster4_Functional_Logic.wording: Normally, WAX is a mixture of additive and complementary logic.

Cluster4_Functional_Logic.title: Ambivalence Measure
Cluster4_Functional_Logic.wording: The difference between the additive and complementary result measures ambivalence in decision-making behavior.

Cluster4_Functional_Logic.title: Threshold Logic
Cluster4_Functional_Logic.wording: Behavior only occurs if WAX exceeds a context-dependent threshold value.

Cluster4_Functional_Logic.title: Non-Linearity
Cluster4_Functional_Logic.wording: There is a non-linear relationship (S-curve) between WAX and actual behavior.

Cluster4_Functional_Logic.title: Interdependence
Cluster4_Functional_Logic.wording: The contributions of the utility types are interdependent and non-separable.

Cluster4_Functional_Logic.title: Asymmetry
Cluster4_Functional_Logic.wording: Negative utilities (Losses) have a stronger effect on WAX than positive utilities.

Cluster4_Functional_Logic.title: Diminishing Returns
Cluster4_Functional_Logic.wording: Additional increases in utility have a diminishing effect on WAX.

Cluster4_Functional_Logic.title: Self-Coherence and Willingness to Act
Cluster4_Functional_Logic.wording: WAX reacts to the dissonance between self-image (I_t) and social feedback (S_t). Small dissonances lead to willingness to learn and adapt, large dissonances lead to blockade and protective behavior. The axiom connects identity coherence with momentary action energy.

definition.interpretation: WAX increases when moderate self-image deviations trigger learning impulses, but decreases when dissonance threatens identity. Thus, $\Delta I_t$ forms a coupling variable between IDN (self-image) and the probability of action.

meta.author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Kernel Team

Cluster5_Complementarities.title: Individual Utility × Awareness
Cluster5_Complementarities.wording: Individual utility only works if it is saliently activated by Awareness.

Cluster5_Complementarities.title: Collective Utility × Uncertainty
Cluster5_Complementarities.wording: Collective utility is sensitive to uncertainty, as coordination becomes uncertain.

Cluster5_Complementarities.title: Identity Utility × Complexity
Cluster5_Complementarities.wording: With increasing complexity, identity norms become stronger as a decision heuristic.
Cluster5_Complementarities.formula: U_IDN^eff = δ * U_IDN, δ > 1 with high complexity

Cluster5_Complementarities.title: INU × IDN
Cluster5_Complementarities.wording: Individual and identity utility can mutually reinforce or block each other.

Cluster5_Complementarities.title: KNU × IDN
Cluster5_Complementarities.wording: Collective norms and identity usually act complementarily.

Cluster5_Complementarities.title: Norm Blockade
Cluster5_Complementarities.wording: Strong norms can completely block high individual utility.

Cluster5_Complementarities.title: Institutional Reinforcement
Cluster5_Complementarities.wording: Strong institutions stabilize WAX against shocks.

Cluster5_Complementarities.title: Uncertainty × Complexity
Cluster5_Complementarities.wording: High uncertainty in complex contexts increases the influence of identity and norms.
Cluster5_Complementarities.formula: λ ↑, if UNS high ∧ KOM high

Cluster6_Integration.title: Upstream Inputs
Cluster6_Integration.wording: WAX necessarily requires the inputs from INU (7234), KNU (7235), IDN (7236), and AWX (7240).

Cluster6_Integration.title: Core Transformation
Cluster6_Integration.wording: WAX transforms utility types and context into momentary willingness to act.
Cluster6_Integration.formula: WAX = f(INU, KNU, IDN, AWX, UNS, KOM, INST)

Cluster6_Integration.title: Downstream Outputs
Cluster6_Integration.wording: WAX delivers outputs to SEG (7257), JNY (7256), and WTX (7259).

Cluster6_Integration.title: Monitoring Interfaces
Cluster6_Integration.wording: WAX is a core indicator in the Intervention Toolkit (9250) and the Watchdog Module (9251).

Cluster6_Integration.title: Crosslinks
Cluster6_Integration.wording: WAX is linked to Uncertainty (9485 ff.), Complexity (9492), and Institutions (9493 ff.).

Cluster6_Integration.title: Feedback to Awareness
Cluster6_Integration.wording: WAX influences future Awareness and changes norm salience.

Cluster6_Integration.title: Life Course Integration
Cluster6_Integration.wording: WAX changes over life phases and is linked to LCP (7457).

Cluster7_Segments.title: Segment WAX
Cluster7_Segments.wording: Each segment receives its own WAX value, which is calculated from the specific parameters.
Cluster7_Segments.formula: WAX_SEG = f(INU_SEG, KNU_SEG, IDN_SEG, AWX_SEG, λ_SEG)

Cluster7_Segments.title: Segment Heterogeneity
Cluster7_Segments.wording: Segments differ in Awareness, utility structure, and λ.

Cluster7_Segments.title: Linear Segment Aggregation
Cluster7_Segments.wording: Macro-WAX can be represented as a weighted average of the segment WAX values.

Cluster7_Segments.title: Network Aggregation
Cluster7_Segments.wording: With strong networking, aggregation is not linear but depends on diffusion and interdependence.

Cluster7_Segments.title: Segment Interdependence
Cluster7_Segments.wording: Changes in one segment influence neighboring segments via network effects.

Cluster7_Segments.title: Segment Paths
Cluster7_Segments.wording: Segments can pass through different paths in the Behavioral Change Journey.

Cluster7_Segments.title: Tipping Points Between Segments
Cluster7_Segments.wording: If critical segments tip, other segments can follow (domino effect).

Cluster7_Segments.title: Segment Specialization
Cluster7_Segments.wording: Certain segments drive change (innovators), others slow it down (traditionalists).

Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.title: Deterministic Dynamics
Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.wording: The change in λ follows deterministic functions of Awareness, Uncertainty, and Complexity.

Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.title: Stochastic Dynamics
Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.wording: In addition to deterministic trends, random shocks occur that can lead to jumps in λ.

Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.title: Tipping Points
Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.wording: If Awareness or social norms exceed a threshold, λ abruptly tips towards additive.
Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.formula: λ(t+1) = λ(t) - Δ, falls AWX ≥ θ

Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.title: Rebound
Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.wording: After a change, λ can fall back to the old state if institutions are weak.

Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.title: Stabilization
Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.wording: Strong institutions stabilize λ long-term and reduce fluctuations.

Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.title: Life Phases
Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.wording: λ changes systematically over the life phases.

Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.title: Path Dependence
Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.wording: The dynamics of λ are dependent on the previous path and are not completely reversible.

Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.title: Coordinated Transition
Cluster8_Dynamics_Transition.wording: Simultaneous changes in multiple segments amplify the dynamics.

Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.title: Indirect Measurement
Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.wording: WAX is not directly observable but must be inferred via indicators such as surveys, choice experiments, or observed behavior.

Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.title: Ambivalence Measurement
Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.wording: Ambivalence can be empirically measured via variance in behavior or intransitive choice patterns.

Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.title: Estimation of λ
Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.wording: The value of λ is estimated by empirically testing differences between additive and complementary logic.

Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.title: Segment Calibration
Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.wording: The estimation of WAX and λ is carried out segment by segment to make heterogeneity visible.

Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.title: Validation
Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.wording: The predictive quality of WAX is checked by correlation with observed behavior.

Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.title: Time Series Measurement
Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.wording: WAX must be recorded via time series to make dynamics and transitions visible.

Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.title: Experimental Manipulation
Cluster9_Measurability_Calibration.wording: Causality can be tested via targeted experiments on Awareness, Uncertainty, or Complexity.

Cluster10_Intervention.title: Intervention Lever
Cluster10_Intervention.wording: WAX can be influenced by changes in Awareness, Uncertainty, Complexity, as well as financial or social incentives.
Cluster10_Intervention.formula: INT: {ΔAWX, ΔUNS, ΔKOM, INC_fin, INC_soc} → ΔWAX

Cluster10_Intervention.title: Threshold Condition
Cluster10_Intervention.wording: An intervention only works if a context-dependent threshold value is exceeded.

Cluster10_Intervention.title: Non-Linearity
Cluster10_Intervention.wording: The effect of interventions increases disproportionately as soon as the threshold is exceeded.
Cluster10_Intervention.formula: ΔWAX = f(INC), increasing for INC ≥ θ

Cluster10_Intervention.title: Segment Dependency
Cluster10_Intervention.wording: Interventions have different strengths of effect in different segments.

Cluster10_Intervention.title: Backfire Effect
Cluster10_Intervention.wording: In contexts with strong norms, financial incentives can strengthen norms and increase λ.
Cluster10_Intervention.formula: INC_fin → λ ↑ if Norm Strength high

Cluster10_Intervention.title: Temporal Effect
Cluster10_Intervention.wording: Interventions take effect with a time delay; short-term effects differ from long-term effects.

Cluster10_Intervention.title: Combined Interventions
Cluster10_Intervention.wording: Combinations (e.g., Awareness + social incentives) are more effective than single measures.

Cluster10_Intervention.title: Feedback Effect
Cluster10_Intervention.wording: Interventions not only change WAX but also feed back into Awareness and norm salience.

Cluster11_Master_Formula.title: Overall WAX Formula
Cluster11_Master_Formula.wording: The overall formula summarizes all axioms from A4 (Clusters 1–10) and operationalizes WAX in BCM 2.0.

formula.Effective_Utility: U_i_eff = α_i * γ_i(UNS) * δ_i(KOM) * U_i * S_i(AWX)
formula.Segments: WAX_macro = Σ ω_s * WAX_seg[s] or f(Network(WAX_seg))
formula.Lambda_Dynamics: dλ/dt = α * AWX - β * UNS - γ * KOM + σ dB_t
formula.Intervention: ΔWAX = f(ΔAWX, ΔUNS, ΔKOM, INC_fin, INC_soc)

Cluster12_System_Integration_Simulation.title: System Integration & Simulation (Meta-Axioms)
Cluster12_System_Integration_Simulation.purpose: This cluster describes the meta-axiomatics of BCM2_06_WAX. It integrates all axioms 1–11 into a time-dependent system logic and uses the simplified uncertainty proxy $UNS_{eff}$ to simulate willingness to act over time.

meta_formula.expression: WAX_sim(t) = F(ΔAWX_t, ΔUNS_eff_t, ΔKOM_t, λ_t, SEG_state_t, INT_t)
meta_formula.description: Time-dynamic aggregation of the WAX axioms. Behavior over time results from changes in the central influencing factors.

meta_axioms.title: Time Dynamics of the WAX Function
meta_axioms.wording: The temporal change in WAX results from the derivatives of the influencing factors Awareness, Uncertainty, Complexity, and Intervention.

meta_axioms.title: Path Dependence of λ
meta_axioms.wording: The hybrid parameter λ changes over time depending on the Awareness, Uncertainty, and Complexity dynamics.
meta_axioms.formula: dλ/dt = α * AWX - β * UNS_eff - γ * KOM

meta_axioms.title: Feedback Rule Between WAX and Awareness
meta_axioms.wording: WAX influences future Awareness. Increasing willingness to act increases the probability that a topic remains salient.
meta_axioms.interpretation: Increased willingness to act stabilizes Awareness over time.

meta_axioms.title: Stability Condition
meta_axioms.wording: The system is stable when the variance of WAX remains within a context-dependent limit value.

parameters.theta_stab: Limit value for permissible volatility of willingness to act

simulation_engine.iteration_scheme: WAX_(t+1) = WAX_t + ΔWAX_t + ε_t, ε_t ~ N(0, σ^2)

Cluster12_System_Integration_Simulation.notes: Cluster 12 operationalizes the meta-axiomatics of BCM3.0. The meta-formula functions as a higher-order axiom and maps the dynamic system behavior of WAX with the integration of the uncertainty proxy $UNS_{eff}$.

A5_Requirements.purpose: This chapter defines the operative, data-related, and contextual requirements for the calculation and simulation of BCM2_06_WAX using the Uncertainty Proxy $UNS_{\text{eff}}$.

inputs.description: These modules provide the central utility types and the Awareness filter as input for the WAX function.

context_variables.description: Context variables modulate discounting (γ), amplification (δ), and the hybrid factor (λ), thereby determining the momentary willingness to act.

segment_parameters.purpose: These parameters define λ_SEG and make differences in willingness to act and intervention efficiency visible.

awareness_salience.description: Awareness determines which utility types are salient and enter the WAX function.

dynamics_time.description: The time dimension ranges from instantaneous reactions (System 0) to institutionally stabilized behavioral patterns.

intervention_parameters.description: Parameters for planning and simulation of interventions in Module 9250 INT.

measurement.validation: All empirical data is calibrated segment-wise (Cluster 10 Measurability) and monitored by 9251 WATCHDOG.

A5_Requirements.notes: A5_Requirements v5.5 integrates the proxy uncertainty family (UNS_eff), expands the time dimension to include 'Instant,' and links WAX to Modules 9250 (Intervention) and 9251 (Governance).

A6_Integration.purpose: This chapter describes the structural, functional, and time-dynamic integration of module 7243_WAX into the architecture of BCM 3.0. It defines upstream and downstream relationships, governance links, and feedback effects, considering the aggregated uncertainty proxy $UNS_{\text{eff}}$.

upstream.description: These modules provide utility types and the Awareness filter, which form the input basis for the calculation of WAX.

core.description: WAX transforms the utility types and context variables into momentary willingness to act and serves as the central transition variable between utility logic and behavior.

downstream.description: Downstream modules use WAX to control the Behavioral Change Journey (JNY), segment logic (SEG), and probability function (WTX).

monitoring.description: Monitoring and intervention control are carried out via 9250 (Intervention Toolkit) and 9251 (Watchdog). Both modules monitor $\Delta WAX$, λ-dynamics, and the stability of the system.

crosslinks.description: These modules provide additional context dimensions that modulate the discounting, amplification, and stability of the WAX value.

feedback_loops.forward: WAX_t influences future Awareness (AWX_(t+1)) and norm salience.
feedback_loops.reverse: Changes in AWX, UNS_eff, or KOM directly feed back into WAX.
feedback_loops.temporal: ΔWAX_t is transferred into temporal simulations via Cluster 12 (WAX_(t+1) = WAX_t + ΔWAX_t + ε_t).

integration_logic.meta_formula: WAX = f(INU, KNU, IDN, AWX, UNS_eff, KOM, INST, λ)

A6_Integration.notes: A6_Integration v5.5 replaces the individual dimensions of the uncertainty family with the aggregated proxy UNS_eff and fully links WAX with the meta-axiomatics of Cluster 12 and the governance modules 9250 and 9251. Feedback loops and stability conditions are simulated dynamically.

A7_Boundaries.purpose: This chapter defines the theoretical, methodological, and operational boundaries of the applicability of BCM2_06_WAX, integrating the dynamic and stochastic components of BCM 3.0.

core: WAX ≠ Preference Function (no long-term utility ordering)
Not a long-term model, but a momentary state (t-dependent)
No self-intervention; changes only via upstream or context variables
No simple aggregation without segment logic (7257_SEG)
No substitution of the utility modules INU/KNU/IDN or the AWX filter
extended: WAX is not a stable disposition but a temporally fluctuating system variable
Simulation results are context- and path-dependent (λ-dynamics)
WAX cannot be interpreted without UNS_eff (proxy required)
No use as an individual performance metric or psychological test score
delimitations.description: Delimitations ensure the formal consistency of WAX within the BCM architecture and prevent faulty reinterpretations outside of utility and context logic.

contextual: Highly context- and time-dependent (WAX_t varies across segments and epochs)
Susceptible to distortions from uncertainty and complexity changes (UNS_eff, KOM)
Backfire effects possible in contexts with strong norms or incorrectly set incentives
technical: Stochastic fluctuations (ε_t) can lead to short-term instabilities
Results depend on the quality and granularity of the input data
Simulation results are sensitive to λ initial values and segment weightings
governance: Only valid within licensed BCM environments (FehrAdvice & Partners AG)
constraints.description: Constraints define the conditions under which WAX is reliably applicable, both empirically and simulatively.

validation_conditions.coherence: WAX consistent with {INU, KNU, IDN, AWX} within defined error tolerance ε < 0.05
validation_conditions.governance_event: WAX_BOUNDARY_ALERT upon violation of stability or coherence conditions

A7_Boundaries.notes: A7_Boundaries v5.5 extends the classical delimitations with dynamic, stochastic, and governance-related constraints. It establishes compatibility with Cluster 12 (System Integration) and the monitoring mechanisms of the Watchdog Module 9251.

A8_Versioning.purpose: This chapter documents the formal development logic of the module BCM2_06_WAX – Willingness to Act from its original additive version (v1.0) to the current meta-axiomatics (v5.5) within the BCM 3.0 architecture.

versions.label: Additive Base Model
versions.core_change: Introduction of WAX as a pure summation function of salient utility without context integration.

versions.label: Hybrid Model with λ
versions.core_change: Introduction of the λ-logic for mixing additive and complementary decision structures.

versions.label: Context and Dynamics Integration
versions.core_change: Introduction of the variables Uncertainty (UNS), Complexity (KOM), and Institutions (INST) with time dynamics.
versions.structure: dλ/dt = α * AWX - β * UNS - γ * KOM

versions.label: Segment Logic & Network Aggregation
versions.core_change: Introduction of segment-specific λ values (λ_SEG) and network aggregation (Macro-WAX).

versions.label: Uncertainty Family & Ambiguity
versions.core_change: Integration of the Uncertainty Family (9485 ff.) and the Ambiguity Module (10180 UNS_AMB).
versions.structure: γ_i = f(UNS_ENV, UNS_IPN, UNS_INS, UNS_EPI, UNS_AMB)

versions.label: Proxy Integration & Meta-Axiomatics
versions.core_change: Introduction of the aggregated Uncertainty Proxy (UNS_eff) and the Meta-Axioms (Cluster 12) for dynamic simulation.
versions.structure: WAX_sim(t) = F(ΔAWX_t, ΔUNS_eff_t, ΔKOM_t, λ_t, SEG_state_t, INT_t)

version_control.maintainer: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Kernel Team

A8_Versioning.notes: A8_Versioning v5.5 represents the consolidated development of the WAX module—from additive logic (v1.0) through hybrid and segment logic (v2.0–v4.0) to proxy integration and meta-axiomatics (Cluster 12). This version forms the basis for audit, simulation, and governance processes in BCM 3.0.
